pathway.title: WABASH NATIONAL Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings no longer cover the debt, so cash burn is the central credit risk. Reported EBITDA was negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, while cash interest of USD 22.82 million is a fixed claim, so interest is being paid from liquidity rather than from operations. The loss is narrowing, with quarterly reported EBITDA improving from negative USD 44.92 million in Q4 2025 to negative USD 6.42 million in Q3 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

Liquidity is adequate for now but was rebuilt with new debt and asset sales rather than by operations. Issuer-stated liquidity was USD 277.0 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 235.3 million at 2025 year end, after USD 150.0 million of convertible notes and USD 39.72 million of asset sale proceeds in nine months, while net debt rose USD 60.04 million to USD 470.97 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

The maturity profile is back-ended, but the revolver springs ahead of the 2028 notes, so refinancing is the dated credit event. No principal falls due before the USD 400 million 4.50% Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15, yet the revolver's maturity is the earliest of several dates, one of which is 91 days before those notes mature, 2028-07-16, less than 20 months from the as-of date. The issuer's debt note puts the Senior Notes at 92.88% of principal on third-party pricing that it says may not reflect daily market activity, and it has not decided how to address the maturity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C06; calculation C07

Margins are the weakest dimension, because cost has risen faster than sales while volumes recovered. Gross margin fell from 19.64% in FY2023 to 1.64% in nine months 2026, and the Transportation Solutions segment's gross result moved by negative USD 47.61 million in nine months although trailer shipments rose 13.4%, which the issuer attributes to material cost, labour and overhead, truck body mix and production-readiness cost brought forward from 2027. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–52; calculation C02; calculation C04

Order intake is the strongest support, but it is not yet earnings. Twelve-month backlog of USD 1,114 million equals 73.37% of last twelve months net sales against 37.34% at 2025 year end, and total backlog of USD 1,198 million is 70% above year end. The issuer opened its 2027 dry van orders early, but it also says some orders may be ahead of tariff-related price increases and that backlog can be changed or cancelled. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; calculation C03

Business risk sits in new trailers, with limited offset from parts and services. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales, Parts & Services was 15.53% of external sales and earned USD 15.52 million, and the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales with none above 10%, so concentration is moderate but cyclicality is not diversified away. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

Financial policy is mixed and the book equity cushion is thin. Dividends of USD 10.03 million were paid in nine months 2026 against an operating loss of USD 97.68 million, repurchases stopped in 2026 but USD 93.2 million of authorization remains, and tangible equity was USD 2.21 million at 2026-09-30; no sponsor, exchange or priming transaction is documented. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

Cost and capex flexibility partly offsets the weak margins. Capital spending including revenue generating assets was USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026 against USD 103.74 million in FY2023, two plants were idled and Goshen was sold for about USD 17.8 million, and operating lease payments of USD 33.69 million and raw material commitments of USD 55.81 million are modest next to liquidity, so cash can be preserved if volumes disappoint. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation C01; calculation C11

The primary downside path is backlog failing to convert while fixed cost has been added for 2027 volumes. At the last twelve months free cash flow burn, liquidity above the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test would last 15.55 months from 2026-09-30, and at the nine-month 2026 burn 22.44 months, which brackets the 2028-07-16 revolver date; this is arithmetic before dividends, not a forecast. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05

cells.text: WABASH NATIONAL Corp (Wabash National Corporation), a Delaware company with principal executive offices in Lafayette, Indiana, listed on the New York Stock Exchange as WNC; consolidated reporting entity with its subsidiaries

Designs, manufactures and services dry freight and refrigerated trailers, platform and tank trailers, dry and refrigerated truck bodies, composite panels, aerodynamic products and food-grade process equipment, and sells aftermarket parts and services; strategy aims to add recurring revenue through parts, Trailers as a Service and the Linq digital marketplace

Two reportable segments: Transportation Solutions (van, platform and tank trailers, truck bodies, wood flooring) and Parts & Services (aftermarket parts, truck body upfitting, process systems, composites, Wabash Parts LLC, Linq and Trailers as a Service)

Sales of new equipment through factory-direct accounts, mainly large fleets, and independent dealers; parts and services follow the installed base; trailer demand is a direct function of freight to be transported

18 independent van trailer dealers with about 55 locations, 32 platform dealers with about 70 locations, 5 tank dealers with 14 locations, more than 1,100 truck body partners and more than 45 independent parts and service locations

Five largest customers were 35%, 42% and 32% of net sales in FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023; no customer above 10% in FY2025; the largest customer was 15% in FY2024 and 12% in FY2023; international sales under 10% of net sales

Total backlog USD 1,198 million and 12-month backlog USD 1,114 million at 2026-09-30, against USD 705 million and USD 576 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 829 million and USD 658 million at 2025-09-30; orders can change or be cancelled

Manufacturing in the United States and one site in Mexico; Little Falls, Minnesota and Goshen, Indiana were idled under a plan announced 2026-01-05 and Goshen was sold in Q3 2026; about 4,700 employees at 2025-12-31, essentially all non-union
Steel, aluminum, plastic and wood from a limited number of suppliers; some price changes are fixed by contract or hedged and cost increases pass to customers with occasional delays

Q3 2026 net sales USD 476,408 thousand, up 24.8% on Q3 2025, with trailer shipments up 43.3% and truck body shipments down 45.1%; nine-month 2026 segment operating result: Transportation Solutions loss, Parts & Services profit

runs.text: The credit has five supports that matter, ranked by how directly they reduce default pressure over the next two years.

- Liquidity and the absence of principal due before 2028 give the issuer time to reach positive cash flow. Issuer-stated liquidity of USD 277.0 million at 2026-09-30 and a debt stack with no principal until 2028-10-15 mean that interest and operating burn can be funded for some time, which lowers near-term default pressure. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

- The order book recovered sharply, which supports 2027 volumes and operating leverage. Total backlog of USD 1,198 million, 70% above year end, and twelve-month backlog covering 73.37% of last twelve months net sales mean that revenue visibility is better than a year ago, provided orders convert and are not cancelled. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; calculation C03

- Cost and capex flexibility allows cash to be preserved. Capital spending fell to USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026, two plants were idled and Goshen sold, and few fixed commitments sit outside debt, so management has levers if volumes disappoint. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation C01

- Customer and channel concentration is moderate. The five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales and none exceeded 10%, with sales split between factory-direct accounts and independent dealers, so the loss of one account would not break the credit. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

- Governance does not add event risk. No sponsor, exchange offer, priming or fee leakage is documented, the audit opinion is unqualified and controls are reported effective, which limits event risk for creditors. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
The credit has five constraints, ranked by how directly they raise default or refinancing risk.

- Earnings and free cash flow are negative. Reported EBITDA of negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow of negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 mean that no leverage multiple exists and that debt service depends on liquidity, which raises refinancing risk with every quarter of burn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

- Margins are very thin and falling in the trailer segment. Gross margin of 1.64% in nine months 2026 against 19.64% in FY2023, and a negative USD 47.61 million move in trailer segment gross result despite higher shipments, mean that volume recovery alone may not restore profit. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C02; calculation C04

- The 2028 refinancing is the dated event and the revolver springs ahead of it. USD 400 million of Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15 and the revolver can mature on 2028-07-16, so committed liquidity and the largest maturity fall in the same window. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; calculation C06

- Tangible equity is thin while dividends continue. Tangible equity of USD 2.21 million at 2026-09-30 leaves almost no book cushion under USD 550.0 million of debt principal, and USD 10.03 million of dividends were paid in nine months 2026 despite an operating loss. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

- Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product with a small offset. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales and Parts & Services only 15.53% of external sales, so the parts business cannot yet cushion a trailer trough. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The main new debt issue is the USD 150.0 million of 4.00% convertible senior unsecured notes due 2032, completed on 2026-07-20 after the initial purchasers exercised a USD 20.0 million option on 2026-07-16. The notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the 4.50% Senior Notes, carry an initial conversion price of about USD 16.75 per share, a 32.50% premium to the USD 12.64 closing price on 2026-07-15, cannot be redeemed before 2029-08-06 except in a cleanup redemption, and convert into about 21.98% of the shares now outstanding if every holder converted at the initial rate. The net proceeds were used primarily to repay revolver borrowings, and the revolver had no amounts outstanding at 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05

The revolving credit agreement was amended twice. The Fifth Amendment on 2026-07-14 allowed up to USD 150.0 million of convertible notes as additional permitted debt. The Sixth Amendment on 2026-08-12 cut commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million, moved the scheduled maturity from 2027-09-23 to 2031-08-12 subject to earlier tests tied to other debt, kept a USD 175 million accordion and raised the margin range over term SOFR from 1.25% to 1.75% to 1.50% to 2.00%. The amended agreement also carries a USD 40 million availability block until fixed charge coverage exceeds 1.0x and a minimum liquidity of USD 90 million, neither of which the previous quarter's description of the agreement mentions. The Senior Notes of USD 400 million remain outstanding to 2028-10-15, and the issuer says it may evaluate alternatives for that maturity without a final decision. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_wnc-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C06

Other transactions were small. Linq was bought out on 2026-01-01 for USD 6.4 million cash and USD 18.6 million of a forgiven note, TrailerHawk.ai assets were bought on 2025-02-03, trailers were sold to a third party on 2026-02-26 with a 24-month limited guaranty of the lessee, and the idled Goshen plant was sold in Q3 2026 for about USD 17.8 million. No sponsor, buyout, merger or change of control transaction is disclosed, and the company states no pro forma figures for any of these events. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Source readiness for WABASH NATIONAL Corp (wnc-879526), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period. The scope is whether the five supplied filings can support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, and which other work they cannot support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five supplied filings are enough to run a credit snapshot of WABASH NATIONAL Corp to Q3 2026, but not to test covenant definitions, ratings or market pricing, because no executed debt agreements, agency ratings or market quotes were supplied. Creditor protections can therefore be described only as the issuer summarises them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Audited annual statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and quarterly statements through the quarter ended 2026-09-30 let net debt, liquidity and trailing twelve month figures be built from primary documents. Nothing dated after the latest filing on 2026-10-29 was supplied, so events up to the 2026-11-18 cutoff are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Period coverage fits the pathway. Two annual reports supply FY2023 to FY2025, three quarterly reports supply Q1, Q2 and Q3 of 2026 with 2025 comparatives, and the FY2025 annual report prints quarterly sales and profit for 2025, so Q4 2025 and the twelve months to Q3 2026 can be derived without a further document. The quarterly cash flow statements are year to date, so discrete Q2 and Q3 cash flows need subtraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt disclosure is instrument level for all three debt instruments: the 4.50% unsecured senior notes due 2028, the 4.00% convertible notes due 2032 issued in July 2026, and the secured revolving credit agreement, which was amended in August 2026 to cut commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million and to extend maturity to 2031. The revolver carries a minimum liquidity test of USD 90 million until a springing fixed charge coverage test takes over, and the issuer reports compliance with all covenants at the latest quarter end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Period comparability needs care before any trend is read. The 2024 results carry a USD 450 million product liability charge in general and administrative expense, and the 2025 results book a USD 418.6 million gain against it after a settlement that insurance covered apart from a USD 30 million company contribution. The Linq business has been consolidated since 2026-01-01 with purchase accounting still provisional, although the filing states that its revenue and earnings are not material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Several inputs that a longer pathway would use are absent: no agency rating, no trading level for the notes, no company earnings guidance, no peer set and no portfolio were supplied. The only price indication is the fair value of the notes in the debt fair value note, which rests on third-party pricing that the issuer says generally does not represent daily market activity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Board composition, committee structure, beneficial ownership and executive pay are incorporated by reference from proxy statements that were not supplied, so Business & governance rests on the annual report's business description and executive officer list.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the ready view is that covenant tests, guarantee and security terms and the springing maturities of the revolver rest on the issuer's own summaries, so a definition in the executed agreements could change the headroom reading. The credit agreement and both indentures would move Legal & covenants from conditional to ready, and a rating report or note quotes would do the same for Ratings & triggers and Market-implied risk. A filing after the 2026-10-29 report that changes debt, liquidity or litigation would also change the latest-quarter view.

fields.value: - The run settings carry no assumptions, ratings, quotes, peers, deal terms, portfolio, legal documents, earlier run or management bridge, so blank values are treated as missing, never as zero.

fields.value: Financial foundation for WABASH NATIONAL Corp as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is FY2023 to FY2025 and the three 2026 quarters with 2025 comparatives: reported EBITDA derived from statement lines, carrying-value debt, net debt, liquidity, last twelve month metrics and the maturity profile.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings no longer cover the debt: reported EBITDA for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 is negative USD 100.36 million, so leverage cannot be stated and creditors depend on liquidity of USD 277.0 million against net debt of USD 470.97 million.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C01; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

fields.value: Reported EBITDA of USD 366.24 million for FY2025 is inflated by a USD 418.6 million litigation gain and would be negative USD 52.36 million without it, so the reported leverage of 1.21x for that year is not a usable signal. Net debt is USD 470.97 million, against USD 281.66 million at FY2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying EBITDA has fallen in each year since FY2023. Reported EBITDA was USD 357.27 million in FY2023, negative USD 299.12 million in FY2024 and USD 366.24 million in FY2025, but FY2024 carries a USD 450 million product liability charge and FY2025 a USD 418.6 million gain on the same matter. Excluding both items, EBITDA falls from USD 357.27 million to USD 150.88 million to negative USD 52.36 million, as net sales fall from USD 2,536.50 million to USD 1,946.74 million to USD 1,542.75 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The loss is narrowing from a low base. Reported EBITDA was negative USD 44.92 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, negative USD 37.33 million in Q1 2026, negative USD 11.69 million in Q2 2026 and negative USD 6.42 million in Q3 2026, so the trend is better but the latest quarter is still below zero. The twelve month figure of negative USD 100.36 million still carries the weak fourth quarter of 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow, not only earnings, is draining the balance sheet. Operating cash flow was negative USD 65.82 million for the nine months to 2026-09-30 even after payables and accruals rose USD 99.11 million, and capital spending of USD 9.19 million was small; USD 39.72 million of asset sale proceeds and the convertible notes bridged the gap. Cash interest of USD 22.82 million over the twelve months is a fixed claim on that same cash.

Net debt rose USD 60.04 million in the nine months because cash burn, fees and dividends exceeded asset sale proceeds; the convertible notes repaid revolver borrowings and changed the debt mix more than the net total.

fields.value: Maturities are back-ended but the revolver springs. No principal falls due before 2028-10-15, when USD 400.0 million of senior notes mature; the revolver was cut from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million and extended to 2031 in August 2026, but it matures 91 days before the senior notes or the convertible notes mature, so the 2028 refinancing governs access to the only committed liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 277.0 million is the issuer's cash plus available revolver capacity, of which USD 69.29 million is cash; it was USD 165.1 million at 2026-03-31 and USD 235.3 million at FY2025, and rose after the convertible notes repaid revolver borrowings rather than because operations produced cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Funding that is not debt is mixed. Customer deposits fell from USD 26.45 million at FY2025 to USD 17.99 million and chassis converter pool financing fell from USD 59.60 million to USD 21.73 million, both inside other accrued liabilities, while accounts payable rose from USD 145.74 million to USD 246.18 million, so suppliers are funding more of the business than customers are.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a turn is order intake and a narrowing loss: total backlog is USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 705 million at FY2025, trailer shipments for the nine months rose year on year, and quarterly EBITDA losses have narrowed for three consecutive quarters. That evidence would win if quarterly EBITDA turns positive while the backlog converts at stable prices, and it would lose if the cost base and tariffs keep gross margin thin or if the early orders prove to be pull-forward ahead of price increases, which the issuer itself notes. Two quarters of positive reported EBITDA would justify a leverage reading; a further fall in liquidity would confirm the negative one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance for WABASH NATIONAL Corp (wnc-879526), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, issuer history and transactions through the Q3 2026 report, and sponsor and governance behaviour as far as the five supplied filings show it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WABASH NATIONAL Corp is a publicly listed trailer and truck-body manufacturer with no identified controlling owner or sponsor, so creditors rely on a cyclical operating business and on a board that kept paying dividends through a loss-making 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is Medium. Repurchases fell from USD 76.21 million in FY2023 to USD 33.77 million in FY2025 and none were made in the first nine months of 2026, and the audit opinion is unqualified. Against that, dividends of USD 10.03 million were still paid in nine months 2026 against an operating loss of USD 97.68 million, USD 150.0 million of convertible debt was added in July 2026 and the revolver was cut from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes leveraged-buyout style extraction risk but also means no sponsor equity support is documented. The issuer is a Delaware company listed on the New York Stock Exchange with one class of common stock, and beneficial ownership percentages and board control rights sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so concentration of control is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is cyclical equipment manufacturing, and the Parts & Services business that management positions as less cyclical is still too small to offset the trailer loss. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales and the Transportation Solutions segment lost USD 58.79 million at the operating line, while Parts & Services earned USD 15.52 million on 15.53% of external sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Order intake has turned sharply upward but is not yet earnings. Total backlog was USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 705 million at 2025 year end, and management attributes the rise to orders exceeding shipments and an early 2027 dry van order cycle. The filing adds that some orders may reflect customers ordering ahead of tariff-related price increases and that backlog can change or be cancelled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration is moderate. The five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales against 42% in FY2024, no customer exceeded 10% in FY2025 after one reached 15% in FY2024, and sales go through factory-direct accounts and independent dealers with international sales under 10%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have been scaled back but not stopped, which is mixed behaviour for creditors. In FY2025 dividends and repurchases together of USD 47.55 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 11.67 million while cash fell by USD 83.56 million, and in nine months 2026 dividends of USD 10.03 million were paid while operating cash flow was negative USD 65.82 million. USD 93.2 million of repurchase authorisation remains until February 2027, and the filings do not state the funding source of either payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 97–98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C07; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The July and August 2026 transactions extended maturities but added debt and tightened the revolver. The issuer sold USD 150.0 million of 4.00% convertible senior unsecured notes due 2032 and repaid revolver borrowings, then cut revolver commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million and moved the stated maturity from 2027 to 2031. The revolver's stated maturity is the earliest of several dates, one of which is 91 days before the USD 400 million 4.50% Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15, which is 2028-07-16, and no final decision on those notes is disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Affiliate and venture exposure is small today but carries contingent claims. The issuer now owns Linq outright after funding it through a note, holds 20% stakes in two venture-lab companies, guarantees a counterparty's equipment lease for 24 months, and has maximum exposure of USD 12.4 million on the UpLabs arrangement and USD 5.8 million on FreightVana. The partner in the Wabash Parts joint venture holds a put right that would require the issuer to buy its 50% interest at a valuation that is not disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 109–110; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality is adequate and creditor-adverse transactions are not found in the five filings. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements and on internal control, disclosure controls were reported effective at 2026-09-30, and no exchange, consent solicitation, covenant waiver, priming or sponsor fee appears in them. The 2024 jury award of USD 450 million, settled in 2025 with a USD 30 million company contribution, shows that litigation can create a very large claim before insurance and appeals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Senior management continuity is a watch item. A new chief financial officer was appointed on 2024-09-01, new chief operating and chief commercial officers on 2025-01-15, and a transition agreement dated 2026-04-08 with the executive listed as chief growth officer in the annual report has terms that were not supplied, so continuity of the team that must deal with the 2028 notes is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is the order book. Total backlog of USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 is 70% above year end 2025, 2027 dry van order books opened early and trailer shipments rose 13.4% in nine months 2026 on higher dry van and platform shipments, so earnings could recover fast enough to make the dividend and any restored buyback unremarkable and support a Low rating. Against that, truck body shipments fell 50.4% in nine months 2026, the trailer segment still lost money, and part of the order surge may be tariff-driven pull-forward. The view would move to High if the proxy statement showed a concentrated holder or entrenched board control, if dividends or buybacks were funded from the revolver while the 2028 maturity approaches, or if the executed credit documents showed wide restricted-payment capacity that was then used. It would move to Low if backlog converted into positive operating cash flow, the 2028 notes were refinanced and no further support to affiliates appeared.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting, which holds director independence, committee membership, beneficial ownership and the related-person policy, was not supplied, so the Medium rating rests on documented behaviour and a concentrated holder or weak board independence would raise it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and both indentures were not supplied, so capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and extra debt is known only from issuer summaries, and the reading that shareholder returns are mixed rather than adverse could change once the baskets are read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Terms of the 2026-04-08 transition agreement and executive pay are not disclosed, so management continuity is judged only from appointment dates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer-level pricing, contract length and the share of backlog under long-term agreements are not disclosed, so the quality of the USD 1,198 million backlog cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main new debt issue is the USD 150.0 million of 4.00% convertible senior unsecured notes due 2032, completed on 2026-07-20 after the initial purchasers exercised a USD 20.0 million option on 2026-07-16. The notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the 4.50% Senior Notes, carry an initial conversion price of about USD 16.75 per share, a 32.50% premium to the USD 12.64 closing price on 2026-07-15, cannot be redeemed before 2029-08-06 except in a cleanup redemption, and convert into about 21.98% of the shares now outstanding if every holder converted at the initial rate. The net proceeds were used primarily to repay revolver borrowings, and the revolver had no amounts outstanding at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The revolving credit agreement was amended twice. The Fifth Amendment on 2026-07-14 allowed up to USD 150.0 million of convertible notes as additional permitted debt. The Sixth Amendment on 2026-08-12 cut commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million, moved the scheduled maturity from 2027-09-23 to 2031-08-12 subject to earlier tests tied to other debt, kept a USD 175 million accordion and raised the margin range over term SOFR from 1.25% to 1.75% to 1.50% to 2.00%. The amended agreement also carries a USD 40 million availability block until fixed charge coverage exceeds 1.0x and a minimum liquidity of USD 90 million, neither of which the previous quarter's description of the agreement mentions. The Senior Notes of USD 400 million remain outstanding to 2028-10-15, and the issuer says it may evaluate alternatives for that maturity without a final decision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_wnc-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions were small. Linq was bought out on 2026-01-01 for USD 6.4 million cash and USD 18.6 million of a forgiven note, TrailerHawk.ai assets were bought on 2025-02-03, trailers were sold to a third party on 2026-02-26 with a 24-month limited guaranty of the lessee, and the idled Goshen plant was sold in Q3 2026 for about USD 17.8 million. No sponsor, buyout, merger or change of control transaction is disclosed, and the company states no pro forma figures for any of these events.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, WABASH NATIONAL Corp presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the continued payment of dividends and the earlier repurchases while operating cash flow was weak, which matters because cash leaves ahead of a 2028 refinancing and implies a small, mixed drain rather than extraction. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, fee, exchange or priming history, an unqualified audit opinion and the USD 1,198 million backlog. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit documents and the terms of the 2026 transition agreement. Business & governance completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Key gaps: board and ownership detail, restricted payment capacity and management transition terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for WABASH NATIONAL Corp (wnc-879526), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated credit view of business risk, financial profile, refinancing and downside, built from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: WABASH NATIONAL Corp is a cyclical manufacturer in an earnings trough whose creditors rely on liquidity and back-ended maturities rather than on operating cash flow, so the credit hinges on converting a rebuilt order book into cash before the 2028 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA was negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, yet issuer-stated liquidity is USD 277.0 million and no principal falls due before 2028-10-15, when USD 400 million of Senior Notes mature. The revolver can mature 91 days earlier, so the committed liquidity that bridges the trough is tied to the same refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings no longer cover the debt, so cash burn is the central credit risk. Reported EBITDA was negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, while cash interest of USD 22.82 million is a fixed claim, so interest is being paid from liquidity rather than from operations. The loss is narrowing, with quarterly reported EBITDA improving from negative USD 44.92 million in Q4 2025 to negative USD 6.42 million in Q3 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for now but was rebuilt with new debt and asset sales rather than by operations. Issuer-stated liquidity was USD 277.0 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 235.3 million at 2025 year end, after USD 150.0 million of convertible notes and USD 39.72 million of asset sale proceeds in nine months, while net debt rose USD 60.04 million to USD 470.97 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The maturity profile is back-ended, but the revolver springs ahead of the 2028 notes, so refinancing is the dated credit event. No principal falls due before the USD 400 million 4.50% Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15, yet the revolver's maturity is the earliest of several dates, one of which is 91 days before those notes mature, 2028-07-16, less than 20 months from the as-of date. The issuer's debt note puts the Senior Notes at 92.88% of principal on third-party pricing that it says may not reflect daily market activity, and it has not decided how to address the maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C06; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are the weakest dimension, because cost has risen faster than sales while volumes recovered. Gross margin fell from 19.64% in FY2023 to 1.64% in nine months 2026, and the Transportation Solutions segment's gross result moved by negative USD 47.61 million in nine months although trailer shipments rose 13.4%, which the issuer attributes to material cost, labour and overhead, truck body mix and production-readiness cost brought forward from 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–52; calculation C02; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Order intake is the strongest support, but it is not yet earnings. Twelve-month backlog of USD 1,114 million equals 73.37% of last twelve months net sales against 37.34% at 2025 year end, and total backlog of USD 1,198 million is 70% above year end. The issuer opened its 2027 dry van orders early, but it also says some orders may be ahead of tariff-related price increases and that backlog can be changed or cancelled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk sits in new trailers, with limited offset from parts and services. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales, Parts & Services was 15.53% of external sales and earned USD 15.52 million, and the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales with none above 10%, so concentration is moderate but cyclicality is not diversified away.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is mixed and the book equity cushion is thin. Dividends of USD 10.03 million were paid in nine months 2026 against an operating loss of USD 97.68 million, repurchases stopped in 2026 but USD 93.2 million of authorization remains, and tangible equity was USD 2.21 million at 2026-09-30; no sponsor, exchange or priming transaction is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility partly offsets the weak margins. Capital spending including revenue generating assets was USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026 against USD 103.74 million in FY2023, two plants were idled and Goshen was sold for about USD 17.8 million, and operating lease payments of USD 33.69 million and raw material commitments of USD 55.81 million are modest next to liquidity, so cash can be preserved if volumes disappoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation C01; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is backlog failing to convert while fixed cost has been added for 2027 volumes. At the last twelve months free cash flow burn, liquidity above the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test would last 15.55 months from 2026-09-30, and at the nine-month 2026 burn 22.44 months, which brackets the 2028-07-16 revolver date; this is arithmetic before dividends, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the turn may already be under way. Quarterly reported EBITDA losses have narrowed for three consecutive quarters, Q3 2026 trailer shipments rose 43.3% and net sales 24.8%, the issuer sold USD 150.0 million of convertible notes in 2026 after exercise of the full over-allotment option, the revolver is undrawn, and forecasters expect 2027 industry production 30.10% and 16.34% above their 2026 estimates. If backlog converts at stable prices and fixed cost is absorbed, reported EBITDA could turn positive and the 2028 refinancing would then depend mainly on market access. The view would improve on two consecutive quarters of positive reported EBITDA with positive operating cash flow, or on an extension of the 2028 notes or the revolver; it would worsen if total backlog fell back toward the USD 705 million of year end 2025, if the revolver were drawn to fund dividends, or if liquidity moved toward the USD 90 million minimum.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer's covenant definition of liquidity, its borrowing base and its fixed charge coverage definition were not supplied, so headroom against the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test cannot be measured and the runway illustrations of 15.55 months and 22.44 months could be longer or shorter in practice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings give no company guidance, rating or trading level, so the outlook rests on third-party industry forecasts and on the debt note's fair value of the Senior Notes, which the issuer says may not reflect daily market activity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Backlog is stated without customer, price or margin detail, so the conversion of USD 1,198 million of orders into cash earnings could be weaker than the revenue coverage ratio suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No guarantor and non-guarantor financial information is printed, so the structural position of the unsecured notes behind non-guarantor subsidiaries and the secured revolver cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit has five supports that matter, ranked by how directly they reduce default pressure over the next two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and the absence of principal due before 2028 give the issuer time to reach positive cash flow. Issuer-stated liquidity of USD 277.0 million at 2026-09-30 and a debt stack with no principal until 2028-10-15 mean that interest and operating burn can be funded for some time, which lowers near-term default pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The order book recovered sharply, which supports 2027 volumes and operating leverage. Total backlog of USD 1,198 million, 70% above year end, and twelve-month backlog covering 73.37% of last twelve months net sales mean that revenue visibility is better than a year ago, provided orders convert and are not cancelled.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cost and capex flexibility allows cash to be preserved. Capital spending fell to USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026, two plants were idled and Goshen sold, and few fixed commitments sit outside debt, so management has levers if volumes disappoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer and channel concentration is moderate. The five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales and none exceeded 10%, with sales split between factory-direct accounts and independent dealers, so the loss of one account would not break the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance does not add event risk. No sponsor, exchange offer, priming or fee leakage is documented, the audit opinion is unqualified and controls are reported effective, which limits event risk for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit has five constraints, ranked by how directly they raise default or refinancing risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings and free cash flow are negative. Reported EBITDA of negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow of negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 mean that no leverage multiple exists and that debt service depends on liquidity, which raises refinancing risk with every quarter of burn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margins are very thin and falling in the trailer segment. Gross margin of 1.64% in nine months 2026 against 19.64% in FY2023, and a negative USD 47.61 million move in trailer segment gross result despite higher shipments, mean that volume recovery alone may not restore profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C02; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2028 refinancing is the dated event and the revolver springs ahead of it. USD 400 million of Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15 and the revolver can mature on 2028-07-16, so committed liquidity and the largest maturity fall in the same window.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Tangible equity is thin while dividends continue. Tangible equity of USD 2.21 million at 2026-09-30 leaves almost no book cushion under USD 550.0 million of debt principal, and USD 10.03 million of dividends were paid in nine months 2026 despite an operating loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product with a small offset. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales and Parts & Services only 15.53% of external sales, so the parts business cannot yet cushion a trailer trough.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wabash designs, manufactures and services dry van, refrigerated, platform and tank trailers, truck bodies and composite products, and sells aftermarket parts and services through two reportable segments. Last twelve months net sales were USD 1,518.33 million, sold through factory-direct accounts to large fleets and through independent dealers, so cash flow follows fleet replacement cycles rather than contracted recurring revenue. The business model supports debt service only when trailer orders are strong: backlog gives visibility for twelve months, but orders can be changed or cancelled and the parts and services business that management expects to be less cyclical is small.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wabash is a publicly listed company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor identified, so there is no sponsor backstop and no sponsor-driven recapitalisation risk, and the governance rating is Medium because shareholder returns continued through losses. The Senior Notes and Convertible Notes are guaranteed by domestic restricted subsidiaries and rank behind a revolver secured on substantially all personal property of the borrowers and guarantors, while the notes are structurally junior to any debt of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them, such as foreign subsidiaries, but no such debt and no guarantor financial information is printed to size that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is volume-driven, cyclical, discretionary and moderately concentrated, with price increases passed on but occasionally with delay. Trailer demand follows the amount of freight to be carried, new trailer shipments rose 13.4% in nine months 2026 while truck body shipments fell 50.4%, and the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales. Because pricing power is limited by customers that know lifecycle costs and by imports, volume recovery supports revenue but margin recovery depends on cost, which is why revenue durability is judged average and margin stability weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins cannot be defended under further volume pressure or cost inflation. Gross margin was 3.12% in Q3 2026 against 4.12% in Q3 2025 even though net sales rose 24.8%, because material cost, labour and overhead rose with volume, truck body mix and low production volumes hurt profitability, and dry van lines were staffed for 2027 volumes ahead of the production they are meant to serve. Operating leverage should work in reverse if volumes recover, but fixed cost, input cost and tariff exposure on steel, aluminum and components mean that the benefit is not quantified in the filings and credit cannot rely on it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation C02; calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and flexible, but EBITDA does not translate into free cash flow because EBITDA is negative. Capital spending was USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026, receivables rose USD 78.1 million and days sales outstanding were 38 days against 35 days a year earlier, while payables and accrued liabilities rose USD 99.1 million, so suppliers funded the working capital build; interest payments of USD 24.18 million fall due in 2027 on fixed-rate notes. Free cash flow before dividends and acquisitions was negative USD 75.01 million for the nine months, so debt service, deleveraging and refinancing support all depend on the earnings recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; calculation C01; calculation C09; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competition matters for credit only where it affects margin, cash flow or refinancing capacity. Each force is assessed on that basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rivalry is intense and price-sensitive. Trailer makers compete on quality, customer relationships, technology and price, and other makers pursue composite sidewalls that compete directly with the issuer's own panels, which limits pricing power and keeps margins thin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The threat from new entrants is mainly imports. A coalition including Wabash petitioned in November 2025 on van-type trailer imports from China, Canada and Mexico; duty orders now cover China while Canada and Mexico remain pending, so relief from import pressure is partial and not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Substitution risk is mainly composite sidewalls from competitors against the issuer's own panels and the option for cautious fleets to defer purchases; the filings give no data on trailer age or deferral, so the effect on volumes is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Buyer power is moderate. Large fleets know lifecycle costs, the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales and the largest was 15% in FY2024, so buyers can hold back orders and press price when freight is weak.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supplier power is meaningful. A limited number of suppliers provide steel coil, aluminum, axles, suspensions and tires, shortages or tariffs raise cost, and increases are passed on with delay, which compresses margin when prices rise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material: tariffs and trade remedies affect material cost, supply chains, competitive conditions and customer purchasing, and the issuer says recent orders may reflect customers buying ahead of tariff-related price increases, which could pull demand forward and then leave a gap. Economic factors are material because the freight cycle sets trailer demand: the 2025 annual report described a continuing freight recession, while the latest quarterly report cites improving freight market fundamentals and accumulated replacement needs. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: a rebuilt order book, liquidity of USD 277.0 million with no principal until 2028-10-15, and low capital needs give the credit time and flexibility, which lowers near-term default pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses: negative EBITDA and free cash flow, gross margin of 1.64%, thin tangible equity of USD 2.21 million and a 73.9% share of new trailers in sales constrain debt service and make the credit dependent on a cyclical recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities: converting backlog at stable prices, absorbing the fixed cost added for 2027 volumes, and trade remedies on imports could restore positive EBITDA and open the 2028 refinancing on better terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats: tariff pull-forward followed by cancellations, further weakness in truck bodies, input cost inflation and an unaddressed 2028 maturity with a springing revolver could drain liquidity before earnings recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate but cyclical. Scale is average at USD 1,518.33 million of last twelve months net sales, the competitive position rests on patented panel technology and a dealer network but earns thin margins, and diversification is limited by the 73.9% share of new trailers. The financial profile is weak and improving only at the margin: cost and capex flexibility is average, margin stability is weak, free cash flow stability is weak, liquidity is average because USD 277.0 million is meaningful but burn and a USD 40 million availability block remain, ability to refinance is average because the 2026 convertible notes show market access while the 2028 notes are unaddressed, and financial policy is average because dividends continue but there is no sponsor and no creditor-adverse transaction. The main supports are liquidity, back-ended maturities and the order book; the main constraints are negative cash flow and the springing revolver; the trend is narrowing losses; and the missing datapoints are the borrowing base, covenant definitions, an issuer EBITDA and any rating or trading level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C01; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the order book is the main tailwind and tariffs, truck bodies and margins are the headwinds. Forecasters expect 2026 United States trailer production 3% and 5% above 2025 and 2027 production 30.10% and 16.34% above their 2026 estimates, backlog supports early 2027 production, and duty orders on Chinese imports are in force, but part of the order surge may be tariff-driven, truck body shipments fell 50.4% in nine months 2026, and the issuer is carrying production-readiness cost ahead of volumes. Over three to five years the same forecasters expect production in 2029 to be 58.67% and 47.52% above their 2026 estimates, which the issuer calls generally consistent with historical levels, so a recovery would restore volume, but the forecasts have been revised before and the filing says actual production may differ materially.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside begins with orders that are cancelled or deferred after the early 2027 order cycle, for example because customers pulled demand forward ahead of tariff price increases. The first operational break is the dry van lines that were staffed and prepared for higher 2027 production, which would run under-absorbed while truck bodies stay weak, so gross margin would stay near the 3.12% of Q3 2026 and reported EBITDA would remain negative. Free cash flow would stay near the USD 144.30 million twelve month burn or the USD 75.01 million nine-month burn, so liquidity above the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test would last between 15.55 and 22.44 months from 2026-09-30, which brackets the 2028-07-16 revolver date and ends before the Senior Notes could be refinanced from earnings. Management levers are limited capital spending already near USD 9.19 million for nine months, suspension of the USD 0.08 per share quarterly dividend, the unused repurchase authorization, further asset sales and cash that could be released from working capital, with receivables of USD 198.61 million and inventory of USD 195.33 million at 2026-09-30, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall through most of 2027 but not sufficient to reach the 2028 maturities without an earnings recovery or an extension.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, WABASH NATIONAL Corp presents an adequate but highly cyclical business profile supported by a rebuilt order book, back-ended maturities and USD 277.0 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by negative earnings, a gross margin of 1.64% and tangible equity of USD 2.21 million. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to free cash flow of negative USD 144.30 million over the last twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on converting backlog into positive reported EBITDA and operating cash flow before the revolver can mature on 2028-07-16, and on market access for USD 400 million of Senior Notes. The primary downside path is backlog failing to convert while fixed cost has been added for 2027 volumes. A comparison with sector peers is not established because no peer set was supplied. Further analysis would require the borrowing base, covenant definitions and executed credit documents, an issuer EBITDA, guidance, ratings and trading levels. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the 2028 refinancing and the springing revolver maturity before earnings recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C01; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Money is in USD millions unless stated and ratios are printed to two decimals, half up. Rows C01 and C11 restate figures from Financial foundation and Business & governance without change; every other row works new arithmetic from the operands shown.
